questions.explanation: Each term doubles the one before: 2, 4, 8, 16, 32. In formula form u_5 = 2 x 2^(5 - 1) = 2 x 16 = 32 - four multiplications by r, one per jump, not five.
questions.prompt: What is the 5th term of the geometric progression 2, 4, 8, 16, ...?

questions.explanation: The partial sums build up one term at a time: S_1 = 2, S_2 = 6, S_3 = 12, S_4 = 20. The pairing formula agrees, because it counts every term in the sum, first to last.
questions.prompt: Find S_4, the sum of the first four terms of the arithmetic progression 2, 4, 6, 8, ...

questions.explanation: A sum to infinity exists because |r| = 1/2 < 1: each term is half the one before, so the running total closes in on 16 without the terms ever needing to stop.
questions.prompt: A geometric progression has first term a = 8 and ratio r = 1/2. Find its sum to infinity.
